crop.notes: The clipping is the end of a long 'Local Gossip' column: a Mafia item, 'A Stage Manager' on thunder effects and W. J. Florence's Memphis story come first; only the last item, 'Ex-Champion Tom Allen' (crop-4 to crop-6), is about Allen. That item is complete.

ocr.notes: Mostly right through the Allen item; the last few lines are garbled ('Lo will be slumbering in, say, ten minutes' and the final sentence are missing or mangled).

title.suggested: Allen Answers 'A Sporting Man' on a Sioux Boxer

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat printed Tom Allen's reply to a reader's idea of putting a Sioux Indian in the prize ring. Allen called pugilism a product of civilization and offered to work the white man's corner.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, January 25, 1891, page 26.

facts.fact: Allen wrote that in pugilism, as in war, the Anglo-Saxon and Celt were superior to all other races, and offered to officiate in the corner of anyone who fought a Sioux Indian
facts.quote: In pugilism, as in war, the Anglo-Saxon and Celt are superior to all other races of men.

notes: The current summary quotes the W. J. Florence item, not the Allen item. Allen's piece also touches on Sullivan-Kilrain, Dempsey-Fitzsimmons, Brettle-Sayers and Broughton-Slack, but only as general boxing talk.
